title: Which city is more crowded, Delhi or Mumbai?
description: Delhi and Mumbai have different areas and different populations. The video finds the number of people for each square kilometre in both cities and compares them to decide which city is more crowded.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare crowding, divide each population by its area to get the people for one square kilometre. Watch for students who compare only the total populations or only the areas.

video_script.why: Two totals cannot be compared when the areas differ, so the population is divided by the area to get the people for one square kilometre.
video_script.substitution: Divide each population by its area, then compare the two results.
video_script.anchor: two crowded cities, Delhi and Mumbai, with their areas and populations, from the book

final_answer.value: Mumbai is more crowded: about 36364 people per sq. km against about 20216 in Delhi
final_answer.spoken: Mumbai is more crowded, with about thirty six thousand three hundred sixty four people for each square kilometre against about twenty thousand two hundred sixteen in Delhi

never_show: Delhi marked as more crowded because it has more people in total
maths_rules: Delhi: 30000000 ÷ 1484 ≈ 20216 people for each sq. km
Mumbai: 20000000 ÷ 550 ≈ 36364 people for each sq. km
check: people 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 times, but land 1484 ÷ 550 ≈ 2.7 times, so Delhi's land grows faster than its people
video_script.design: One idea: the people for one square kilometre decide the crowding. The two city maps stay on the stage and the working sits on the board.
